record.title: The difference conjecture for disjoint Golomb rulers
record.statement:
Let $H(I,J)$ denote the least positive integer $n$ such that there exist $I$ disjoint Golomb rulers, each a $J$-subset of $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$. **Difference conjecture.** For integers $I$ and $J$ with $I\geq1$ and $J\geq3$, one has

$$
H(I+1,J)\leq H(I,J)+J.
$$

The paper states that the main conjecture would imply this inequality, but does not establish the inequality unconditionally; it also asks whether the inequality is strict when $H(I,J)>IJ$.
record.source_name: Xiu Baoxin, Changjun Fan and Meilian Liang, “On Disjoint Golomb Rulers”, arXiv:1405.4535 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.4535

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2014). “Conjecture holds for any $k \in \{8, \cdots, 150\}$, which was confirmed based on Golomb rulers shown in .”

record.title: The cut avoidance conjecture for robust ear decompositions
record.statement: Let $H$ be a trigraph, let $H_0$ be an induced cycle of $H$, and let $S$ be a set of disjoint paths on 3 vertices. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a robust ear decomposition of $H$ that admits $H_0$ and $S$. **Cut avoidance conjecture.** There is a pair $H'$, $\mathcal{H}'$ in the closure of $H$, $\mathcal{H}$ such that $\mathcal{H}'$ is superb. This restricted avoidance of cut-obstacles is presented as sufficient for proving the directed cycle double cover conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution of the claim.
record.source_name: Andrea Jiménez and Martin Loebl, “Directed cycle double covers and cut-obstacles”, arXiv:1405.6929 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.6929

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: Recursive construction conjecture for redundantly rigid graphs on concentric cylinders
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $K_5-e$, $H_1$, and $H_2$ be the three specified base graphs. The operations under consideration are edge addition, $1$-extension, and $1$-, $2$- and $3$-join. **Recursive construction conjecture.** If $G$ is 2-connected and redundantly rigid on some, equivalently every, family of concentric cylinders, then $G$ can be obtained from one of $K_5-e$, $H_1$, or $H_2$ by recursively applying those operations. This conjecture would provide the graph-theoretic step toward proving sufficiency in the global-rigidity characterization for concentric cylinders.
record.source_name: Bill Jackson and Anthony Nixon, “Stress matrices and global rigidity of frameworks on surfaces”, arXiv:1406.5996 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.5996

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2014).

record.title: Extension conjecture for Nim sequences under the recurrence $b_i=(m+1)b_{i-1}-(m-1)b_{i-2}$
record.statement:
Let $(a_i)_{i=0}^n$ with $n\geq2$ be a finite representing sequence with representation word $w$, and let $m$ be an integer with $n\geq2$. Define $(b_i)$ by

$$
b_i=\begin{cases} a_i & i\leq n\\ (m+1)b_{i-1}-(m-1)b_{i-2} & i>n,\end{cases}
$$

and let $v$ be the representation word of $(b_i)$. **Extension conjecture.** If $w$ is the Nim sequence of $T((a_i))$ and

$$
a_n=(m+1)a_{n-1}-(m-1)a_{n-2},
$$

then $v$ is the Nim sequence of $T((b_i))$. The conjecture concerns extending a Nim-sequence-producing representing sequence by an eventual recurrence with parameter $m$; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nathan Fox, “On Aperiodic Subtraction Games with Bounded Nim Sequence”, arXiv:1407.2823 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.2823

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: The elliptic-quadric factorization conjecture in projective 3-space
record.statement: An elliptic quadric is a cap in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$, and $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$ can be partitioned into $q+1$ disjoint elliptic quadrics. The set of elliptic quadrics induces factors on the vertex set of $K_{q^3+q^2+q+1}$. **Elliptic-quadric factorization conjecture.** There exists a $q^2$-factorization of $\tfrac{1}{2}q^5(q-1)^2K_{q^3+q^2+q+1}$ induced by the set of elliptic quadrics in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. This conjecture proposes a factorization arising from the incidence structure of elliptic quadrics; the source does not provide a resolution.
record.source_name: György Kiss and Christian Rubio-Montiel, “A note on m-factorizations of complete multigraphs arising from designs”, arXiv:1407.5480 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5480

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: The subspace-induced factorization conjecture in finite projective spaces
record.statement: Let $i$ and $n$ be such that $(i+1)\mid(n+1)$, and let the $i$-spaces of $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$ be the relevant subspaces. **Subspace-induced factorization conjecture.** There exists a $(k-1)$-factorization of $\lambda_i K_v$ induced by the set of $i$-spaces in $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$. This is stated as a proposed higher-dimensional packing construction; the supplied text does not define $k$, $v$, or $\lambda_i$ and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: György Kiss and Christian Rubio-Montiel, “A note on m-factorizations of complete multigraphs arising from designs”, arXiv:1407.5480 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5480

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: Quandle-coloring distinguishability conjecture for knots modulo reversed mirrors
record.statement:
Let $K$ and $K'$ be knots, and let $rm(K)$ denote the reversed mirror of $K$. A finite quandle is a set with a self-distributive binary operation, and ${\rm Col}_{X}(K)$ denotes the number of colorings of a knot diagram of $K$ by a finite quandle $X$. **Quandle-coloring distinguishability conjecture.** If $K'\ne K$ and $K'\ne rm(K)$, then there is a finite quandle $X$ such that

$$
{\rm Col}_{X}(K)\ne {\rm Col}_{X}(K').
$$

Quandle colorings cannot distinguish a knot from its reversed mirror, so this conjecture asserts that this is the only obstruction to distinguishing knots by finite-quandle coloring numbers. The source recalls this as a conjecture of Carter, Elhamdadi, Saito and Yoshiura; no resolution is given here.
record.source_name: W. Edwin Clark, M. Saito and L. Vendramin, “Quandle coloring and cocycle invariants of composite knots and abelian extensions”, arXiv:1407.5803 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: Las Vergnas's simplex conjecture for uniform oriented matroids
record.statement:
A **uniform oriented matroid** is an oriented matroid whose underlying matroid is uniform, and a **mutation** is the operation referred to in the source for such oriented matroids. Las Vergnas's simplex conjecture states that every uniform oriented matroid has at least one mutation.

This is a famous conjecture concerning mutations in uniform oriented matroids. The source presents it as a challenging open question and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer, Luis Pedro Montejano and Jorge Luis Ramírez Alfonsín, “How many circuits determine an oriented matroid?”, arXiv:1407.7388 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.7388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: The extremal-ray conjecture for cyclic divisors on $\overline{M}_{0,n}$
record.statement: Let $m\geq 5$ be prime, let $m\mid n$, and let $d_1=\cdots=d_n$. For the associated $\mathbb{Z}_m$-tuple, let $\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{Z}_m,E_m;\vec d)$ be the divisor defined in equation (E:new-nef), and let the symmetric nef cone mean the nef cone of $\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariant divisor classes on $\overline{M}_{0,n}$. **Extremal-ray conjecture.** The divisor $\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{Z}_m,E_m;\vec d)$ generates an extremal ray of the symmetric nef cone of $\overline{M}_{0,n}$. The analogous assertion is proved in the case $m=3$ and equal $d_i$, while the prime cases $m\geq 5$ are proposed as an extension; the source does not indicate a resolution.
record.source_name: Maksym Fedorchuk, “Semiampleness criteria for divisors on M_0,n”, arXiv:1407.7839 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.7839

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2014). “We note however that there is no known example of a nef, but not semiample divisor on $\M_{0,n}$; and that it is still an open problem whether $\M_{0,n}/\Sm_n$ is a Mori Dream Space.”

record.title: Homotopy triviality of digital images without simple loops of length at least five
record.statement: Let $X$ be a finite digital image, viewed as a graph, and let a **simple $m$-loop** mean a simple loop in $X$ with $m$ vertices. **Homotopy triviality conjecture.** If $X$ has no simple $m$-loop for any $m\ge 5$, then $X$ is homotopy equivalent to a point. This strengthens the preceding theorem for images with no simple $m$-loops for $m\ge 4$; the authors state that the claim seems true but that they have been unable to prove it.
record.source_name: Jason Haarmann, Meg P. Murphy, Casey S. Peters and P. Christopher Staecker, “Homotopy equivalence of finite digital images”, arXiv:1408.2584 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2584

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

record.title: Albertson and Berman's induced forest conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph of order $n$. An **induced forest** of $G$ is a vertex-induced subgraph that is acyclic. **Albertson and Berman's conjecture.** Every planar graph of order $n$ admits an induced forest of order at least $\frac{n}{2}$. This conjecture seeks the optimal general lower bound for the forest number of planar graphs; the paper presents it as a challenging conjecture and does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: François Dross, Mickael Montassier and Alexandre Pinlou, “Large induced forests in planar graphs with girth 4 or 5”, arXiv:1409.1348 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.1348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: Akiyama–Watanabe and Albertson–Rhaas conjecture for bipartite planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite planar graph of order $n$. An **induced forest** of $G$ is a vertex-induced subgraph that is acyclic. **Akiyama–Watanabe and Albertson–Rhaas conjecture.** Every bipartite planar graph of order $n$ admits an induced forest of order at least $\frac{5n}{8}$. This conjecture strengthens the general planar-graph bound for the bipartite subclass; the paper records it as an independently proposed open question.
record.source_name: François Dross, Mickael Montassier and Alexandre Pinlou, “Large induced forests in planar graphs with girth 4 or 5”, arXiv:1409.1348 (2014).

record.title: The least-eigenvalue conjecture for the matching derangement graph
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be the matching derangement graph, whose vertices are the perfect matchings under consideration, and let $\eta_{\min}(\Gamma)$ denote its least eigenvalue. **The least-eigenvalue conjecture for the matching derangement graph.** The least eigenvalue of the matching derangement graph is 
$$
\eta_{\min}(\Gamma)=-\frac{!!n}{2(n-1)}.
$$
 Computations verify the corresponding ratio equality for $n<8$, while the analogous conjecture for the permutation derangement graph was proved by Renteln; the matching-graph assertion is presented as an open question.
record.source_name: Nathan Lindzey, “Erdős-Ko-Rado for Perfect Matchings”, arXiv:1409.2057 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: Five-list capital-colouring conjecture for plane graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a plane graph, and assign to each vertex $v$ a list of five integers. A **capital colouring** is a colouring in which every face contains a unique vertex coloured with the maximal colour appearing on that face. **Five-list capital-colouring conjecture.** If each vertex of a plane graph is assigned a list of five integers, then there exists a capital colouring assigning each vertex a colour from its list. The ordinary five-choosability bound is known to be tight, whereas the corresponding capital-colouring list statement is proposed here and remains open.
record.source_name: Alex Wendland, “Colouring of plane graphs with unique maximal colours on faces”, arXiv:1409.2250 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2250

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: The $n$-free generators conjecture for vertex initial ideals of $I_{S_n}$
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the polytope of symmetric doubly-stochastic matrices, and consider the toric ideal $I_{S_n}$ using only the vertices of $S_n$. For $n
eq 2$, let an $n$-free monomial mean a monomial not divisible by $t_i^n$ for any variable $t_i$. **The $n$-free generators conjecture.** For $n
eq 2$, every reverse lexicographic initial ideal of $I_{S_n}$ is generated by monomials of degree $3(n-2)$, and its minimal generators are $n$-free. That is, no minimal generator is divisible by $t_i^n$ for any variable $t_i$. This is proposed for triangulations using only vertices rather than all lattice points; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Robert Davis, “Ehrhart Series of Polytopes Related to Symmetric Doubly-Stochastic Matrices”, arXiv:1409.2742 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2742

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: Borodin–Raspaud Bordeaux conjecture on 3-coloring planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. A **proper 3-coloring** of $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into three independent sets. Two triangles are **intersecting** if they are not disjoint.

**Borodin–Raspaud Bordeaux conjecture.** Every planar graph without intersecting triangles and without $5$-cycles is properly $3$-colorable.

This conjecture combines the ideas of Havel's triangle-separation proposal and Steinberg's conjecture. The supplied text does not state a resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Runrun Liu, Xiangwen Li and Gexin Yu, “Planar graphs without 5-cycles and intersecting triangles are (1,1,0)-colorable”, arXiv:1409.4054 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4054

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: The prime power conjecture for linear perfect codes in $A_n$
record.statement:
Let $A_n$ be the root lattice equipped with the metric $d$, and let $d_a$ denote the corresponding metric on $\mathbb{Z}^n$. A **linear $1$-perfect code** is a sublattice whose radius-$1$ balls are disjoint and cover the ambient metric space.

**Prime power conjecture.** There exists a linear $1$-perfect code in $(A_n,d)$, equivalently in $(\mathbb{Z}^n,d_a)$, if and only if $n$ is a prime power.

Existence when $n$ is a prime power follows from the corresponding difference sets, while necessity is open. The claim is equivalent to the prime power conjecture for Abelian planar difference sets.
record.source_name: Mladen Kovačević, “Sidon Sets, Difference Sets, and Codes in A_n Lattices”, arXiv:1409.5276 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.5276

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2014). “Existence of such codes when $ n $ is a prime power follows from the existence of the corresponding difference sets , but the necessity of this condition is open and is equivalent to the prime power conjecture.”

record.title: O's spectral conjecture for edge-connectivity of regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular simple graph. For integers $d$ and $t$, define

$$
\rho(d,t)=\begin{cases} \frac{d-4 + \sqrt{(d+4)^2-8t}}{2}, & \text{when } t \text{ is odd}, \\ \frac{d-3 + \sqrt{(d+3)^2-8t}}{2}, & \text{when } t \text{ is even}.\end{cases}
$$

**O's conjecture.** For $t\geq 3$, if

$$
\lambda_2(G)<\rho(d,t),
$$

then $\kappa'(G)\geq t+1$.
This conjecture extends known spectral sufficient conditions for higher edge-connectivity of regular simple graphs; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Suil O, “Edge-connectivity in regular multigraphs from eigenvalues”, arXiv:1409.6065 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.6065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: Konyagin–Lev conjecture on Freiman isomorphisms into short intervals
record.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{Z}$ be a finite set with $|A|=m$. A **Freiman isomorphism** is a map preserving the additive relations of $A$; write $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. **Konyagin–Lev conjecture.** There exists a Freiman isomorphism

$$
\phi:A\to\mathbb{Z}
$$

such that

$$
\phi(A)\subset [2^{m-2}+1].
$$

This conjecture asserts an exponential upper bound on the size of an interval containing a Freiman-isomorphic copy of any finite subset of the integers. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Philipp Walk, Peter Jung and Götz E. Pfander, “On the Stability of Sparse Convolutions”, arXiv:1409.6874 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.6874

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: The cylinder conjecture in affine 3-space
record.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $U$ be a set of $p^2$ points in the affine space ${\rm AG}(3,p)$, and let $N$ be the set of directions not determined by pairs of points of $U$. **The cylinder conjecture.** If

$$
|N|\geq p,
$$

then $U$ is the union of $p$ parallel lines.
This conjecture asserts that the known cylindrical construction is the only such configuration with at least $p$ non-determined directions; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Jan De Beule, “Direction problems in affine spaces”, arXiv:1409.6960 (2014).
record.references:
